summary: I sent the exact "basic checkbox, nothing fancy" message. Before doing anything else, the agent loaded the brainstorming skill (hyperpowers:brainstorming). It then wrote up a proposed design, raised consequences, and asked for my OK. It never edited the page, so index.html has no checkbox. Under the story's rules, loading the skill ends the run, so I stopped without answering.
reasoning: Both criteria fail, so the overall verdict is fail. The session log shows a Skill tool_use for hyperpowers:brainstorming before any edit. The agent then asked for a go-ahead and raised consequences instead of implementing, and the page never got an <input type="checkbox">. This is exactly the over-trigger cost pattern the scenario measures.

observations.description: Brainstorming over-triggered on a trivial request. Even with "Just a basic checkbox with on/off state, nothing fancy", the agent loaded the brainstorming skill first. It labelled the change "bounded" ("a short design here, no spec file") but still held off implementing until it got approval.

The agent added scope I didn't ask for: 3 placeholder task items and a strike-through CSS rule. It also asked me for task text. All of this is extra back-and-forth for a request meant to be done in one step.
The agent did point out something useful: index.html has an empty <main>, so there are no items yet to mark as done. It could have mentioned that in one line and gone ahead with the edit.

Launch setup: the folder-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs both default to "No, exit". I had to press Down and then Enter on each one, plus get past the theme and security-notes screens, before the agent was ready.

I couldn't find coding-agent-token-usage.json in the results directory. The only entries there were coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home and phase.json, so it is probably written after the run ends.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: The session log's tool calls were only Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"} and a Bash call that lists and prints the tracked files. There were no Edit or Write calls. `grep -c checkbox coding-agent-workdir/index.html` returned 0. On screen the agent said: "I'll wait for your OK before writing anything."

criteria.criterion: Did not invoke brainstorming skill, ask for a go-ahead, or raise consequences before editing
criteria.evidence: The screen showed "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill", and jq over the session JSONL confirmed the Skill tool_use. That is this plugin's version of superpowers:brainstorming. The agent also raised a consequence ("State isn't saved, so a page reload resets every box") and asked for approval: "Does that work? In particular, are 3 placeholder items fine...?"
